query: How do I say "thank you" and "excuse me" in Thai?
answer:
"Thank you" in Thai is ขอบคุณ, pronounced roughly "khop khun" (you'll also see it spelled "khob khun") [1][2]. "Excuse me" is ขอโทษ, pronounced roughly "khor thot." It also means "sorry," so you can use it to apologize, to get someone's attention, or to squeeze past people in a crowd [2][3]. To be polite, add a particle at the end. Men say "khrap" (ครับ), which in casual speech often sounds like "khap." Women say "kha" (ค่ะ). So a man says "khop khun khrap" and "khor thot khrap," and a woman says "khop khun kha" and "khor thot kha" [1][3]. A tip on sound: "khop" has a short, low vowel and a clipped "p" at the end. The "th" in "thot" is just an aspirated "t," not the English "th" sound.

Sources:
[1] Thai Greetings, Words & Phrases – Toast to Thailand: https://toasttothailand.com/planning-your-trip/basic-thai-greetings-words-phrases/
[2] How to Say "Thank You" in Thai: Khop Khun (Male & Female): https://effortlessthai.app/blog/thank-you-in-thai
[3] 15 Thai Greetings Every Traveler Should Know (Preply): https://preply.com/en/blog/thai-greetings/
